title: Возвращение старого официанта  (Return of the Former Waiter)

segments.t: At Claude Monet, Max muses on the strange laws of the universe that bring people from the past back into our lives. Right on cue, handsome former waiter Ilya walks into the kitchen and greets the veterans while waiting to ask Vika for his old job back.
Не знаю, по каким законам вселенная это работает.
Возвращается жизнь, которую ты мог потерять.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
Не знаю, по каким законам вселенная это работает.
'I do not know by what laws of the universe this works.' Pointing out that he does not know by what laws of the universe this works gives Senya a sobering reality check.
'Just as it seemed to you.' With the room and kitchen in play, Vika keeps this short reply brisk and direct. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Возвращается жизнь, которую ты мог потерять.

'The life you could have lost comes back to you.' Realizing that the life Barinov could have lost comes back to Barinov changes how Senya handles the situation. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'But sometimes a return happens.' Noting that sometimes a return happens keeps Barinov's side of the story simple and clear.

'Are you a new guy here or what?' Here checking whether Barinov a new guy here shows Vika looking for the real truth. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'Here you go!' Senya declares that here Barinov goes as the tension in the room peaks. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
'Senya, how is the fricassee coming along.' Saying that how is the fricassee coming along is how Barinov sets the tone with Senya.
'Wait, who is that?' With the shift and kitchen hanging in the air, Vika puts Barinov on the spot. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.

'He used to work here as a waiter.' Adding that he used to work here as a waiter fills in the missing piece for Barinov. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
'He was almost like a son to me.' Barinov tells Senya that he was almost like a son to him without dressing it up.
'Not like you.' Between the kitchen and the job, Vika gives Barinov a quick, grounded response. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.

'Will Viktoriya Sergeyevna take me back?' Checking whether Viktoriya Sergeyevna take him back is how Senya puts Barinov on the spot. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'Ever since you left.' Barinov reminds Senya that ever since Senya left before the moment passes. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Не знаю, по каким законам вселенная это работает.
Возвращается жизнь, которую ты мог потерять.
That wraps up this scene as max reflects on how people from the past suddenly return just as former waiter Ilya walks into Claude Monet hoping Vika will hire him back. Until next time!
